sections.h2: What are the options for selling a house in La Crosse?
sections.html:
La Crosse sellers can list with an agent, sell privately, or take a cash offer from a buyer who accepts the house in its current condition. The Census Bureau estimates 50,784 people lived in the city on July 1, 2025, about 3.6 percent below the April 2020 base of 52,691.

The right route depends on timing and condition. A listing exposes the house to the widest group of buyers, including the faculty and health-care workers who work for the city's large employers. A direct sale fits an owner facing a move, a vacant rental, an estate or repairs they do not want to fund.

sections.h2: What makes La Crosse housing different from other Wisconsin cities?
sections.html:
The geography does. La Crosse sits on a flat prairie on the east bank of the Mississippi, between 500-foot bluffs that belong to the Driftless Area and the coulee country around it. The Black River joins the Mississippi north of town, and the La Crosse River broadens into a marsh that splits the city into a north side and a south side. The city covers 23.79 square miles, and 2.08 of them are water.

The people are different too. The 2020 census counted a median age of 30.7 years, and 3,897 residents lived in college or university housing. About 40.7 percent of households had one person. Only 46.1 percent of households own their home, the lowest rate among Kenosha, Janesville, Greenfield and La Crosse in the Census QuickFacts comparison, so rented housing is a large share of the market.

Climate adds its own checklist. The July average high is 85.4 degrees Fahrenheit and the January average high is 27.4, with a record high of 108. Buyers who inspect a La Crosse house look closely at the furnace, the air conditioning and the basement walls.

sections.h2: Which neighborhoods, schools and employers drive demand in La Crosse?
sections.html:
La Crosse has 13 voting wards, and its neighborhoods include Bluffside, Washburn, Historic Cass and King, Powell-Poage-Hamilton, Historic Downtown, Northside, Grandview Emerson, Weigent Hogan, Hintgen, College Park and Springbrook Clayton Johnson. College Park is the district around the University of Wisconsin-La Crosse campus.

Employers matter more here than in most cities this size. Gundersen Health System and Mayo Clinic Health System (the Franciscan Skemp campus) have their flagship sites here, Kwik Trip is headquartered in the city, and the University of Wisconsin-La Crosse, Viterbo University and Western Technical College bring students and staff. Mention the nearest employer or campus when you describe the house, since proximity to work is what those households ask about.

The School District of La Crosse enrolled 6,139 students in 2022 and runs Central and Logan high schools. Catholic and Lutheran schools, including Aquinas, also operate in the city. Roads include Interstate 90, U.S. 14, 53 and 61, and state highways 35, 16 and 33, and the Cass Street and Cameron Avenue bridges connect downtown with La Crescent, Minnesota. La Crosse Regional Airport offers scheduled service to Chicago.

sections.h2: What rental rules affect a La Crosse house?
sections.html:
La Crosse regulates both long-term and short-term rentals, and an investor who sells a rental house should know which rules apply. Residential rental units are registered with the Planning and Development Department's Building and Inspections office, whose application charges $10 for each parcel (email inspection@cityoflacrosse.org or call 608-789-7530). Ask the office whether the registration stays with the owner or must be redone by the buyer.

Short-term rentals fall under Article XIX of the city code. The ordinance defines them as a residential dwelling rented for a fee for fewer than 30 consecutive days, and a license comes from the City Clerk. A short-term rental license cannot be transferred to a buyer, and no advertisement may run until the required county, state and local permits are in hand. A buyer who plans to run the house as a short-term rental therefore has to apply on their own.

  • Registration of a rental unit: Building and Inspections.
  • Short-term rental license: City Clerk, under Article XIX.
  • Tax account questions: La Crosse County Treasurer, 212 6th Street North, (608) 785-9711, open 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays.

sections.h2: What does recording and transferring a La Crosse house involve?
sections.html:
The seller owes Wisconsin's transfer fee of 30 cents for each $100 of value or fraction thereof, which comes to $540 on a $180,000 sale (Wis. Stat. 77.22). The county register of deeds collects it at recording. Under that statute the grantor and the grantee sign the electronic return, and the register cannot record the deed without it.

Some transfers are free of the fee, including transfers by will or descent and transfers between a parent and child for nominal consideration (Wis. Stat. 77.25). Plan for these steps:

  • Order title work and a payoff letter for any mortgage.
  • File the transfer return with the Department of Revenue and keep the receipt.
  • Record the deed at the La Crosse County Register of Deeds.
  • Settle prorated taxes at closing.

sections.h2: What disclosure and tax rules apply to a La Crosse seller?
sections.html:
An owner of a property with one to four dwelling units delivers a completed Real Estate Condition Report within 10 days after the buyer's contract is accepted. If the report is late, the buyer has two business days after the tenth day to rescind and recover any deposit (Wis. Stat. 709.02). Executors and trustees who never lived in the house are excused.

Real estate tax is payable on or before January 31 and July 31 in two equal parts, unless the total bill is under $100 (Wis. Stat. 74.11). Delinquent amounts are paid to the county treasurer with interest and penalties charged from the preceding February 1. Because the next date is January 31, 2027, ask the treasurer for the current balance before you set a closing date.

faqs.q: How long does it take to sell a house in La Crosse?
faqs.a: It depends on the route. A listing moves at the pace of showings, inspection and lender approval, while a direct sale can close as soon as the title work and the transfer return are done. Ask your title company to estimate the schedule after you have a signed contract.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to sell a La Crosse rental house?
faqs.a: Rental units are registered with the Building and Inspections office, which charges $10 per parcel on its application. Short-term rental licenses come from the City Clerk and cannot be transferred, so a buyer applies on their own.

faqs.q: What does the transfer fee cost in La Crosse?
faqs.a: It is 30 cents per $100 of value or fraction thereof, charged to the seller. A $150,000 house carries a fee of $450, collected by the county register of deeds when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in La Crosse?
faqs.a: Payments made on or before January 31 go to the local taxation district treasurer and later payments go to the county treasurer. The La Crosse County Treasurer is at 212 6th Street North and can be reached at (608) 785-9711.

faqs.q: Can an estate sell a La Crosse house without a condition report?
faqs.a: A personal representative, trustee or court-appointed fiduciary who has never occupied the house is excused from the report under chapter 709. The sale still needs a deed, a transfer return and any exemption language the register requires.
